v-heft.bottom_line: In men with chronic congestive heart failure receiving digoxin and a diuretic, hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate vs placebo reduced cumulative mortality by two years (25.6 percent vs 34.3 percent) with an estimated 34 percent reduction in mortality risk (P<0.028).
v-heft.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate was associated with lower cumulative mortality than placebo through two years (25.6 percent vs 34.3 percent) and an estimated 34 percent reduction in mortality risk (P<0.028; 95 percent confidence interval, 4 to 54 percent), while prazosin showed no mortality difference vs placebo. The study did not provide sufficient data to compare mortality beyond three years.

v-heft-ii.bottom_line: In 804 men with chronic congestive heart failure receiving digoxin and diuretic therapy, enalapril vs hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate reduced mortality after two years (18 percent vs 25 percent; P = 0.016).
v-heft-ii.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, enalapril was associated with lower 2-year mortality than hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate (18 percent vs 25 percent; P = 0.016), with the difference attributed to fewer sudden deaths (e.g., sudden, no warning: 16% vs 25%). The document also reports no difference in pump-failure mortality (23% vs 19%; P = 0.44) and similar heart-failure hospitalization proportions (18.9 percent vs 18.4 percent), so the results do not establish superiority for those outcomes.

save.bottom_line: In patients with left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction, mortality from all causes was significantly reduced with captopril vs placebo (reduction in risk 19 percent; 95 percent confidence interval, 3 to 32 percent; P = 0.019).
save.implications: These data support the conclusion that, in this trial population, captopril vs placebo was associated with lower all-cause mortality (275/1116 vs 228/1115; risk reduction 19%, 95% CI 3 to 32) and lower cardiovascular mortality (234 vs 188; risk reduction 21%, 95% CI 5 to 35). The document does not establish effects in patients outside the enrolled criteria (e.g., those with ejection fraction >40% or with overt heart failure requiring vasodilator therapy).

aire.bottom_line: In survivors of acute myocardial infarction with clinical evidence of heart failure, ramipril versus placebo reduced all-cause mortality with an observed risk reduction of 27% (95% CI 11% to 40%).
aire.implications: Based on the reported intention-to-treat results, this document supports that in this selected post-AMI population with clinical evidence of heart failure, ramipril (vs placebo) was associated with lower all-cause mortality (170 deaths; 17% vs 222 deaths; 23%) and a reported 27% risk reduction (95% CI 11% to 40%). It does not establish effects for patients excluded from the trial (eg, severe heart failure/unstable angina/ACE-inhibitor contraindications) and does not by itself determine effects on specific non-mortality outcomes beyond the reported secondary composite and serious adverse event counts.

woscops.bottom_line: In men with moderate hypercholesterolemia and no history of myocardial infarction, pravastatin vs placebo reduced the risk of definite nonfatal myocardial infarction or death from coronary heart disease by 31% (95% confidence interval, 17 to 43 percent).
woscops.implications: These data support that, over about 5 years, pravastatin compared with placebo reduced definite nonfatal myocardial infarction or death from coronary heart disease (248 (7.9) vs 174 (5.5); risk reduction 31% (17 to 43); P<0.001). They also show a reduction in death from all cardiovascular causes (73 (2.3) vs 50 (1.6); 32% (3 to 53); P=0.033) and no statistically significant difference in death from noncardiovascular causes (62 (1.9) vs 56 (1.7); P=0.54). The document does not establish a statistically significant reduction in death from any cause (P=0.051) and does not show a difference in fatal or nonfatal stroke (P=0.57).

dig.bottom_line: In the main trial, mortality from any cause was similar with digoxin vs placebo (risk ratio when digoxin was compared with placebo, 0.99; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.91 to 1.07).
dig.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, digoxin vs placebo did not change all-cause mortality (0.99; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.91 to 1.07), while it was associated with fewer patients hospitalized for worsening heart failure (26.8 percent vs. 34.7 percent; risk ratio, 0.72; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.66 to 0.79) and more hospitalizations for suspected digoxin toxicity (2.0 vs. 0.9; risk ratio, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.42–3.32).

elite.implications: This 48-week trial in patients aged 65 years or older with symptomatic heart failure and ejection fraction ≤40% shows no difference between losartan and captopril in the prespecified primary renal-dysfunction endpoint (10.5% in each group; risk reduction 2% [95% CI ⫺51% to +36%]). afcaps-texcaps.bottom_line: Lovastatin vs placebo reduced first acute major coronary events (RR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.50-0.79).
afcaps-texcaps.implications: In this trial population, the reported numbers support that lovastatin (20-40 mg/d) vs placebo reduced the incidence of a first acute major coronary event (RR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.50-0.79) over an average 5.2 years, with similar overall mortality (80 vs 77 deaths) and similar rates of serious adverse experiences (34.2% vs 34.1%). cibis-ii.bottom_line: In symptomatic chronic heart failure patients, bisoprolol vs placebo reduced all-cause mortality with a hazard ratio of 0.66 (95% CI 0.54–0.81).
cibis-ii.implications: In this trial of 2647 stable, ambulatory NYHA III–IV patients with left-ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or less, bisoprolol compared with placebo was associated with lower all-cause mortality (156/1327 [11.8%] vs 228/1320 [17.3%]; hazard ratio 0.66 [95% CI 0.54–0.81]) and fewer sudden deaths (48 [3.6%] vs 83 [6.3%]; hazard ratio 0.56 [0.39–0.80]). The document cautions that results should not be extrapolated to patients with severe class IV symptoms and recent instability because safety and efficacy has not been established in these patients.

merit-hf.bottom_line: In MERIT-HF, metoprolol CR/XL once daily vs placebo lowered all-cause mortality (relative risk 0.66 [95% CI 0.53–0.81]).

The document also reports reductions in sudden death (0.59 [0.45–0.78]) and death from aggravated heart failure (0.51 [0.33–0.79]). rales.bottom_line: In patients with severe heart failure, spironolactone vs placebo reduced all-cause mortality (relative risk of death, 0.70; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.82).
rales.implications: In this trial of severe heart failure, spironolactone (25 mg daily, with protocolized dose adjustments) vs placebo was associated with fewer deaths (46 percent vs 35 percent; relative risk of death, 0.70; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.82; P<0.001) and fewer cardiac hospitalizations (336/753 vs 260/515; relative risk, 0.70; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.59 to 0.82; P<0.001). The document also reports increased gynecomastia or breast pain in men (10 percent vs 1 percent; P<0.001) and low reported serious hyperkalemia in both groups (1 percent vs 2 percent). These results are reported for the enrolled population under the stated eligibility/exclusion criteria and follow-up duration, and do not by themselves establish effects outside those criteria.

hope.bottom_line: In high-risk patients, ramipril vs placebo reduced the primary composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes (relative risk, 0.78; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.70 to 0.86).
hope.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, assigning ramipril rather than placebo reduced the risk of the primary composite outcome (14.0% vs 17.8%; relative risk, 0.78; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.70 to 0.86) and reduced several individual outcomes (e.g., death from cardiovascular causes 6.1% vs 8.1%; myocardial infarction 9.9% vs 12.3%; stroke 3.4% vs 4.9%). The results also show higher discontinuation for cough with ramipril (7.3% vs 1.8%). The document does not provide evidence here about effects outside the studied eligibility criteria or beyond the follow-up described.

cure.bottom_line: In patients with acute coronary syndromes without ST-segment elevation, clopidogrel plus aspirin vs placebo plus aspirin reduced the first primary outcome (relative risk, 0.80; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.72 to 0.90).
cure.implications: Based on the reported event rates (9.3% vs 11.4%) and relative risk (0.80; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.72 to 0.90; P<0.001), the document supports that adding clopidogrel to aspirin reduced the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or stroke in this trial population, while major bleeding was increased (3.7% vs 2.7%; relative risk, 1.38; P=0.001); the document also reports no significant excess in life-threatening bleeding (2.2% vs 1.8%; P=0.13).

val-heft.bottom_line: In Val-HeFT, valsartan vs placebo added to background heart-failure therapy reduced the combined end point of mortality and morbidity (relative risk, 0.87; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.77 to 0.97).
val-heft.implications: These results support that, in this trial population, valsartan (vs placebo) reduced the risk of the combined mortality–morbidity end point (relative risk, 0.87; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.77 to 0.97) while not changing all-cause mortality (relative risk, 1.02; 0.88–1.18). They also support that discontinuations due to adverse events were higher with valsartan (9.9 percent vs 7.2 percent).

affirm.bottom_line: In AFFIRM, rhythm-control vs rate-control for atrial fibrillation showed no significant difference in overall mortality (hazard ratio, 1.15 [95 percent confidence interval, 0.99 to 1.34]; P=0.08).
affirm.implications: These data support that, in this population (4060 patients) and follow-up, rhythm-control did not demonstrate a statistically significant mortality benefit over rate-control (hazard ratio, 1.15 [95 percent confidence interval, 0.99 to 1.34]; P=0.08), while hospitalizations were higher with rhythm control (80.1 percent vs. 73.0 percent; P<0.001). Stroke event counts were similar (77 vs 80), and the document reports that most strokes occurred when warfarin was stopped or INR was subtherapeutic; the trial does not establish a reduction in ischemic stroke with rhythm-control.

copernicus.bottom_line: In COPERNICUS, carvedilol vs placebo reduced the combined risk of death or hospitalization for a cardiovascular reason by 27% (95% CI, 16% to 37%).
copernicus.implications: In this trial of 2289 euvolemic patients with severe chronic heart failure (ejection fraction ⬍25%), carvedilol (vs placebo) was associated with lower Kaplan-Meier 1-year cumulative risk of death or hospitalization for a cardiovascular reason (41.6% vs 30.2%) and a reported 27% lower risk (95% CI, 16% to 37%). The document also reports fewer serious adverse events with carvedilol (39.0% vs 45.5%). These findings pertain to the enrolled population (eg, 'but not volume-overloaded') and do not by themselves establish effects in patients who were not enrolled.

ascot-lla.bottom_line: In ASCOT-LLA, atorvastatin 10 mg versus placebo reduced the primary endpoint of non-fatal MI plus fatal CHD (hazard ratio 0.64 [95% CI 0.50–0.83]).
ascot-lla.implications: These data support that, in this hypertensive population with baseline total cholesterol around 5.5 mmol/L, atorvastatin 10 mg was associated with fewer non-fatal MI plus fatal CHD events than placebo (hazard ratio 0.64 [95% CI 0.50–0.83]; 100 vs 154 events). The document also reports reductions in several secondary endpoints (eg, total coronary events 0.71 [0.59–0.86] and fatal/non-fatal stroke 0.73 [0.56–0.96]) while all-cause mortality was not significantly reduced (0.87 [0.71–1.06]). Because the lipid-lowering arm was stopped early after a median 3.3 years, the results reflect this shorter follow-up.

charm-overall.bottom_line: In the CHARM-Overall programme, candesartan vs placebo reduced all-cause mortality with a covariate adjusted hazard ratio of 0.90 (95% CI 0.82–0.99).
charm-overall.implications: These results support that, in this programme, candesartan compared with placebo was associated with lower cardiovascular deaths (691 [18%] vs 769 [20%]) and lower cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF (1150 [30.2%] vs 1310 [34.5%]) with adjusted hazard ratios below 1, while the all-cause mortality reduction was borderline by unadjusted analysis (p=0.055) but statistically significant after covariate adjustment (0.90 [0.82–0.99], p=0.032). The document also reports more discontinuations with candesartan due to renal function concerns, hypotension, and hyperkalaemia, so the findings do not establish benefit without these tolerability trade-offs.

ephesus.bottom_line: In patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by left ventricular dysfunction and heart failure, eplerenone vs placebo reduced death from any cause (relative risk, 0.85; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.75 to 0.96).

europa.bottom_line: In EUROPA, perindopril 8 mg once daily vs placebo reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular mortality, MI, or cardiac arrest with a 20% relative risk reduction (95% CI 9 to 29).
europa.implications: These results support that, in this population, perindopril reduced the composite primary endpoint from 9.9% to 8.0% over 4.2 years (relative risk reduction 20% [95% CI 9 to 29]) and produced a reported 1.9% absolute risk reduction; the document also reports an estimate that about 50 patients would need treatment for 4 years to prevent one major cardiovascular event. The evidence does not establish a statistically significant reduction in cardiovascular mortality alone (14% [–3 to 28], p=0.107) or total mortality alone (11% [–2 to 23], p=0.1) as reported here.

valiant.bottom_line: In high-risk patients after myocardial infarction, valsartan vs captopril had similar all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 1.00; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.90 to 1.11).
valiant.implications: Based on the reported all-cause mortality hazard ratio for valsartan vs captopril (1.00; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.90 to 1.11) and the prespecified noninferiority finding (P=0.004), the results support concluding that valsartan was no less effective than captopril for mortality in this trial population; the reported death counts (979, 958) indicate similar absolute mortality. The combination arm does not support improved survival versus captopril (hazard ratio 0.98; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.89 to 1.09) and is associated with more drug-related adverse events.

a-heft.bottom_line: In A-HeFT, isosorbide dinitrate plus hydralazine vs placebo improved the primary composite score (−0.1±1.9 vs. −0.5±2.0, P=0.01).
a-heft.implications: In this trial of 1050 black patients with advanced heart failure on background therapy, the fixed-dose combination improved the primary composite score (−0.1±1.9 vs. −0.5±2.0; P=0.01) and was associated with lower all-cause mortality (6.2% vs. 10.2%) and fewer first heart-failure hospitalizations (16.4% vs. 24.4%), while headache (47.5% vs. 19.2%) and dizziness (29.3% vs. 12.3%) occurred more often with the combination; these data support benefit within the studied population and follow-up as reported.

cards.bottom_line: In patients with type 2 diabetes without previous cardiovascular disease, atorvastatin 10 mg daily vs placebo reduced the primary endpoint (hazard ratio 0.63 [0.48–0.83]).
cards.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, allocation to atorvastatin 10 mg daily reduced first major cardiovascular events versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.63 [0.48–0.83], p=0.001), with stroke also reduced (0.52 [0.31–0.89]). The mortality result was not statistically significant (0.73 [0.52–1.01], p=0.059), so this document does not license a definite conclusion of reduced all-cause mortality based on CARDS alone.

peace.bottom_line: In stable coronary artery disease with preserved left ventricular function, trandolapril vs placebo did not reduce the primary end point (hazard ratio 0.96; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.88 to 1.06; P=0.43).
peace.implications: With primary end point rates of 21.9% vs 22.5% and a hazard ratio of 0.96 (95% CI, 0.88 to 1.06; P=0.43), these data do not support a reduction in the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal MI, or coronary revascularization from adding trandolapril to therapy in this population; however, the confidence interval remains consistent with both modest benefit and modest harm for the primary end point.

prove-it-timi-22.bottom_line: In patients hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome within the preceding 10 days, 80 mg of atorvastatin daily vs 40 mg of pravastatin daily reduced the primary end point at two years (22.4% vs 26.3%), with a 16% hazard reduction (95% confidence interval, 5 to 26 percent).
prove-it-timi-22.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, high-dose atorvastatin produced a lower 2-year Kaplan–Meier primary end-point rate than standard-dose pravastatin (22.4% vs 26.3%) and was associated with more frequent ALT elevations >3× ULN (3.3% vs 1.1%). The results do not establish the mechanism of benefit or whether differences are due solely to LDL lowering, and they were obtained in a "carefully selected and monitored study population."

major_points.text: Randomized comparison of standard-dose pravastatin vs high-dose atorvastatin after recent acute coronary syndrome.
major_points.quote: We enrolled 4162 patients who had been hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome within the preceding 10 days and compared 40 mg of pravastatin daily (standard therapy) with 80 mg of atorvastatin daily (intensive therapy).

major_points.text: Primary end point was a composite including death, MI, unstable angina rehospitalization, late revascularization, and stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary end point was a composite of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, documented unstable angina requiring rehospitalization, revascularization (performed at least 30 days after randomization), and stroke.

major_points.text: Achieved median LDL differed substantially between arms during treatment.
major_points.quote: The median LDL cholesterol level achieved during treatment was 95 mg per deciliter (2.46 mmol per liter) in the standard-dose pravastatin group and 62 mg per deciliter (1.60 mmol per liter) in the high-dose atorvastatin group (P<0.001).

major_points.text: Primary end point at two years was lower with atorvastatin, and the prespecified equivalence criterion was not met.
major_points.quote: Kaplan–Meier estimates of the rates of the primary end point at two years were 26.3 percent in the pravastatin group and 22.4 percent in the atorvastatin group, reflecting a 16 percent reduction in the hazard ratio in favor of atorvastatin (P=0.005; 95 percent confidence interval, 5 to 26 percent).

major_points.quote: The percentages of patients who had elevations in alanine aminotransferase levels that were more than three times the upper limit of normal were 1.1 percent in the pravastatin group and 3.3 percent in the atorvastatin group (P<0.001).

stellar.bottom_line: In the open-label STELLAR trial, over 6 weeks rosuvastatin 10 to 40 mg reduced non-HDL-C by 42.0% to 50.9% compared with 34.4% to 48.1% with atorvastatin, 26.0% to 41.8% with simvastatin, and 18.6% to 27.4% with pravastatin.
stellar.implications: Over 6 weeks in this open-label trial, the reported least squares mean percentage reductions in non-HDL-C and apo B were larger with rosuvastatin 10–40 mg than with the stated dose comparisons (e.g., non-HDL-C 42.0% to 50.9% vs 34.4% to 48.1% with atorvastatin). These data support conclusions about short-term changes in lipids/apolipoproteins and ratios as reported, but do not establish effects on clinical outcomes in this document ("The studies investigating the impact of rosuvastatin therapy on clinical out-comes are ongoing.").

commit.bottom_line: In 45 852 patients with suspected acute MI, allocation to metoprolol versus placebo did not significantly reduce the co-primary composite outcome (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.90–1.01) or death (OR 0.99, 0.92–1.05) during the scheduled treatment period in hospital.
commit.implications: These results support that, during the scheduled in-hospital treatment period, metoprolol did not produce a statistically significant reduction in the co-primary composite outcome (2166 [9.4%] vs 2261 [9.9%]; OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.90–1.01) or death (1774 [7.7%] vs 1797 [7.8%]; OR 0.99, 0.92–1.05). They also support that metoprolol was associated with fewer reinfarctions (464 [2.0%] vs 568 [2.5%]) and fewer ventricular fibrillation events (581 [2.5%] vs 698 [3.0%]) but more cardiogenic shock (1141 [5.0%] vs 885 [3.9%]) in this setting and timeframe.

charisma.implications: These results support that, in the overall trial population, clopidogrel plus aspirin was not significantly more effective than placebo plus aspirin for the primary composite end point (0.93; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.83 to 1.05; P = 0.22). They also show more moderate bleeding with clopidogrel plus aspirin (2.1 percent vs. 1.3 percent; P<0.001) and no statistically significant increase in severe bleeding (1.7 percent vs. 1.3 percent; P = 0.09).

mega-study.bottom_line: Diet plus pravastatin vs diet alone reduced coronary heart disease (66 events vs 101 events; HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.49–0.91).

euridis-adonis.bottom_line: In the combined EURIDIS/ADONIS trials, dronedarone vs placebo reduced recurrence of atrial fibrillation at 12 months (hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.87).
euridis-adonis.implications: These trials support that, compared with placebo, dronedarone prolonged time to first recurrence and reduced recurrence at 12 months in the combined analysis (hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.87; recurrence rates 64.1% vs 75.2%). triton-timi-38-2007.bottom_line: In patients with acute coronary syndromes with scheduled percutaneous coronary intervention, the primary efficacy end point occurred in 12.1% of patients receiving clopidogrel and 9.9% of patients receiving prasugrel (hazard ratio for prasugrel vs. clopidogrel, 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.90; P<0.001).
triton-timi-38-2007.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, prasugrel reduced the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke versus clopidogrel (9.9% vs. 12.1%; hazard ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.73–0.90) while increasing non–CABG-related TIMI major bleeding (2.4% vs. 1.8%; hazard ratio, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.03–1.68) and fatal bleeding (0.4% vs. 0.1%). It does not establish a significant difference in overall mortality because death from any cause was 188 (3.0) with prasugrel and 197 (3.2) with clopidogrel (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.78–1.16).

andromeda.bottom_line: In patients with severe heart failure, dronedarone vs placebo increased all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.07 to 4.25).
andromeda.implications: These data support that, in this severe heart failure population, dronedarone increased early all-cause mortality versus placebo (8.1% vs 3.8%; hazard ratio, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.07 to 4.25), while the primary composite endpoint was not statistically different (17.1% vs 12.6%; hazard ratio, 1.38; 95% CI, 0.92 to 2.09). The trial’s early termination and small number of deaths limit conclusions about other endpoints beyond the reported estimates.

jupiter.bottom_line: In apparently healthy men and women with LDL cholesterol <130 mg per deciliter and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein ≥2.0 mg per liter, rosuvastatin 20 mg daily vs placebo reduced the primary end point (hazard ratio, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.46 to 0.69).

appraise.bottom_line: Compared with placebo, apixaban 10 mg once daily increased ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (hazard ratio, 2.45; 95% confidence interval, 1.31 to 4.61; P⫽0.005).
appraise.implications: In this phase 2 trial, adding apixaban to antiplatelet therapy increased major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding versus placebo (e.g., apixaban 10 mg once daily HR 2.45, 95% CI 1.31 to 4.61), while ischemic outcomes were numerically lower but not statistically significant (e.g., HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.35 to 1.04; P⫽0.07). These numbers support concluding increased bleeding risk and only a trend (not definitive proof) toward fewer ischemic events at the tested lower doses.

athena.implications: These results support that, in this trial population, dronedarone vs placebo reduced the composite of first hospitalization due to cardiovascular events or death (734 [31.9%] vs 917 [39.4%]; hazard ratio 0.76 [95% CI, 0.69 to 0.84]) and reduced cardiovascular death (63 [2.7%] vs 90 [3.9%]; hazard ratio 0.71 [95% CI, 0.51 to 0.98]) but did not demonstrate a significant reduction in death from any cause (hazard ratio 0.84 [95% CI, 0.66 to 1.08]). The document also reports higher rates of specific adverse events and more discontinuation due to adverse events with dronedarone.

atlas-acs-timi-46.bottom_line: In patients stabilised after an acute coronary syndrome, rivaroxaban versus placebo did not significantly reduce the primary efficacy endpoint (HR 0.79 [0.60–1.05]).
atlas-acs-timi-46.implications: These data support that, versus placebo, rivaroxaban increased clinically significant bleeding in a dose-dependent manner (eg, HR 5.06 [3.45–7.42] for 20 mg) while the primary efficacy endpoint was not statistically different (HR 0.79 [0.60–1.05], p=0.10). The numbers do support a reduction in the main secondary endpoint of death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (HR 0.69 [0.50–0.96], p=0.0270), but the document also states the trial was not powered for efficacy.

heaal.bottom_line: In ACE-inhibitor–intolerant heart failure patients, losartan 150 mg daily versus 50 mg daily reduced the primary composite of death or admission for heart failure (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82–0.99).
heaal.implications: These data support that, in this studied population, losartan 150 mg daily (vs 50 mg daily) was associated with a lower hazard of the composite of death or admission for heart failure (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82–0.99), while some adverse events (eg, renal impairment, hypotension, hyperkalaemia) occurred more often at 150 mg; the trial does not provide a placebo comparison for losartan 50 mg, and it studied patients intolerant to ACE inhibitors.

plato.bottom_line: In PLATO, ticagrelor versus clopidogrel reduced the 12-month primary composite of death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke (hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.77 to 0.92).
plato.implications: These data support that ticagrelor, compared with clopidogrel, was associated with a lower 12-month Kaplan–Meier rate of the composite of death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke (9.8% vs. 11.7%; hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.77 to 0.92) while showing no significant difference in major bleeding by study criteria (11.6% vs. 11.2%; P=0.43), but a higher rate of non–CABG-related major bleeding (4.5% vs. 3.8%; P=0.03). current-oasis-7.bottom_line: In patients undergoing PCI for acute coronary syndromes, double-dose clopidogrel reduced cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke at 30 days versus standard-dose clopidogrel (adjusted hazard ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.74–0.99).
current-oasis-7.implications: In this prespecified PCI subgroup, the reported 30-day data support that double-dose clopidogrel (vs standard-dose) was associated with a lower absolute event rate for cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (3.9% vs 4.5%) with an adjusted HR of 0.86 (95% CI 0.74–0.99), alongside a higher major bleeding rate (1.6% vs 1.1%). The aspirin dose comparison shows similar primary-outcome rates (4.1% vs 4.2%) with an adjusted HR of 0.98 (0.84–1.13), and therefore does not support a difference in the primary composite outcome between high-dose and low-dose aspirin over 30 days in this PCI population.

major_points.text: Double-dose clopidogrel reduced the 30-day primary composite outcome compared with standard-dose clopidogrel.
major_points.quote: Compared with the standard dose, double-dose clopidogrel reduced the rate of the primary outcome (330 events [3·9%] vs 392 events [4·5%]; adjusted hazard ratio 0·86, 95% CI 0·74–0·99, p=0·039)

major_points.text: High-dose versus low-dose aspirin did not differ for the primary outcome.
major_points.quote: High-dose and low-dose aspirin did not diﬀer for the primary outcome (356 [4·1%] vs 366 [4·2%]; 0·98, 0·84–1·13, p=0·76).

major_points.text: Major bleeding was more common with double-dose than with standard-dose clopidogrel.
major_points.quote: Major bleeding was more common with double-dose than with standard-dose clopidogrel (139 [1·6%] vs 99 [1·1%]; 1·41, 1·09–1·83, p=0·009)

plato-2010.bottom_line: In acute coronary syndromes with a planned invasive strategy, ticagrelor vs clopidogrel reduced the primary composite endpoint (hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.75–0.94).

shift-2010.bottom_line: Ivabradine vs placebo reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for worsening heart failure (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.75–0.90).
shift-2010.implications: In this trial population, ivabradine (vs placebo) was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite endpoint (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.75–0.90), with fewer first hospital admissions for worsening heart failure (514 [16%] vs 672 [21%]; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.66–0.83) and fewer deaths from heart failure (113 [3%] vs 151 [5%]; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58–0.94). All-cause mortality did not differ significantly (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.80–1.02). Symptomatic bradycardia and phosphenes occurred more often with ivabradine (150 [5%] and 89 [3%], respectively) than placebo (32 [1%] and 17 [1%], respectively).

appraise-2.bottom_line: In APPRAISE-2, apixaban 5 mg twice daily vs placebo added to standard antiplatelet therapy after acute coronary syndrome did not significantly reduce the primary outcome (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.80 to 1.11) and increased TIMI major bleeding (hazard ratio with apixaban, 2.59; 95% CI, 1.50 to 4.46).
appraise-2.implications: With 279/3705 (7.5%) vs 293/3687 (7.9%) for cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke (hazard ratio 0.95; 95% CI, 0.80 to 1.11; P = 0.51), the document supports that apixaban did not show a statistically significant reduction in recurrent ischemic events in this trial. With TIMI major bleeding 46/3673 (1.3%) vs 18/3642 (0.5%) (hazard ratio 2.59; 95% CI, 1.50 to 4.46; P = 0.001), it supports that adding apixaban increased major bleeding; the text also reports more fatal bleeding (5 vs. 0) and intracranial bleeding (12 vs. 3) with apixaban. Because the trial was stopped early, the document states that certainty about efficacy conclusions is limited.

aristotle.bottom_line: Apixaban versus warfarin reduced stroke or systemic embolism (hazard ratio with apixaban, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.95).
aristotle.implications: Based on the reported hazard ratios and event rates, apixaban compared with warfarin was associated with lower rates of stroke or systemic embolism (1.27% per year vs 1.60% per year; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.95), major bleeding (2.13% per year vs 3.09% per year; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.60 to 0.80), and death from any cause (3.52% per year vs 3.94% per year; HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.99). The document also reports no significant difference for ischemic or uncertain type of stroke (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.13; P = 0.42).

dose.implications: These data support that, over 72 hours, bolus vs continuous infusion did not differ on the coprimary endpoints (global symptom AUC 4236±1440 vs 4373±1404; creatinine change 0.05±0.3 vs 0.07±0.3 mg per deciliter). For high-dose vs low-dose, the symptom AUC difference did not meet conventional statistical significance (P = 0.06), while worsening renal function within 72 hours was more frequent with high-dose (23% vs 14%; P = 0.04); the trial also states it was not powered to detect between-group differences in clinical events.

emphasis-hf.bottom_line: In patients with NYHA class II systolic heart failure, eplerenone vs placebo reduced the primary composite of death from cardiovascular causes or hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.54 to 0.74).
emphasis-hf.implications: These results support that, in this trial population, eplerenone compared with placebo was associated with lower risk of the primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.54 to 0.74) and lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.93), while increasing the proportion of patients with serum potassium >5.5 mmol per liter (11.8% vs 7.2%). The document also states results may not be applicable to all patients with mild symptoms because eligibility required additional risk factors.

re-deem.bottom_line: Compared with placebo, dabigatran was associated with higher major or clinically relevant minor bleeding, with hazard ratio (HR) 4.27 (1.86, 9.81) for 150 mg.
re-deem.implications: These data support that adding dabigatran to predominantly dual antiplatelet therapy increased the 6-month risk of major or clinically relevant minor bleeding in a dose-dependent fashion (e.g., HR 4.27 [1.86, 9.81] at 150 mg vs placebo). The trial reports numerically similar or lower rates of the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-haemorrhagic stroke at higher doses (3.0% and 3.5% at 110 and 150 mg vs 3.8% placebo), but ischaemic endpoints were reported descriptively, so definitive efficacy conclusions are not licensed by these numbers alone.

rocket-af.bottom_line: In this trial comparing rivaroxaban with warfarin in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, the primary end point occurred at 1.7% per year vs. 2.2% per year (hazard ratio 0.79; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.96; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
rocket-af.implications: These data support that rivaroxaban achieved noninferiority to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism in the per-protocol, as-treated analysis (hazard ratio 0.79; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.96; P<0.001 for noninferiority). In the intention-to-treat analysis, noninferiority was also met (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.03; P<0.001 for noninferiority) but superiority was not shown (P = 0.12 for superiority). Major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding did not significantly differ (hazard ratio, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.96 to 1.11; P = 0.44), while intracranial hemorrhage (0.5% vs. 0.7% per year; P = 0.02) and fatal bleeding (0.2% vs. 0.5%; P = 0.003) were lower with rivaroxaban, and major gastrointestinal bleeding was more common with rivaroxaban (3.2% vs. 2.2%, P<0.001).

rocket-af-2011.bottom_line: Rivaroxaban was noninferior to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism (hazard ratio in the rivaroxaban group, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 0.96).
rocket-af-2011.implications: Based on the per-protocol, as-treated analysis, rivaroxaban met noninferiority versus warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism (0.79 [0.66–0.96]). In the intention-to-treat analysis, noninferiority was met (0.88 [0.75–1.03]) but superiority was not (P = 0.12). Major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding was similar (1.03 [0.96–1.11]), while intracranial hemorrhage (0.67 [0.47–0.93]) and fatal bleeding (0.50 [0.31–0.79]) were lower with rivaroxaban and hemoglobin decreases ≥2 g/dl (1.22 [1.03–1.44]) and transfusions (1.25 [1.01–1.55]) were higher.

shift.bottom_line: In SHIFT, ivabradine vs placebo reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for worsening heart failure (HR 0.82 [0.75–0.90]).
shift.implications: These data support that, in SHIFT, ivabradine (vs placebo) lowered the risk of the primary composite outcome (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.75–0.90) and reduced hospital admission for worsening heart failure (16% vs 21%; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.66–0.83), while not demonstrating a statistically significant reduction in all-cause mortality (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.80–1.02; p = 0.092).

atlas-acs-2-timi-51.bottom_line: In patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome, rivaroxaban vs placebo reduced the primary composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke (8.9% vs. 10.7%; hazard ratio 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.96).
atlas-acs-2-timi-51.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, rivaroxaban (combined doses) vs placebo reduced the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke (8.9% vs. 10.7%; hazard ratio 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.96) while increasing TIMI major bleeding not related to CABG (2.1% vs. 0.6%) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.6% vs. 0.2%); the document reports no significant difference in fatal bleeding (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66).

major_points.text: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial in recent acute coronary syndrome patients testing low-dose rivaroxaban twice daily (2.5 mg or 5 mg) vs placebo.

atlas-acs-2-timi-51-2012.bottom_line: In patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome, rivaroxaban reduced the primary efficacy end point versus placebo (8.9% vs. 10.7%; hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.96).
atlas-acs-2-timi-51-2012.implications: These data support that, versus placebo, rivaroxaban was associated with a lower Kaplan–Meier rate of the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke (8.9% vs. 10.7%; hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.96), while being associated with higher rates of TIMI major bleeding not related to CABG (2.1% vs. 0.6%) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.6% vs. 0.2%) and no significant difference in fatal bleeding (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66); the document also reports that the 2.5-mg twice-daily dose reduced cardiovascular and all-cause mortality whereas the 5-mg twice-daily dose did not significantly reduce those mortality outcomes.

ctt-collaborators.bottom_line: Across 27 randomised trials, lowering LDL cholesterol with statin therapy reduced major vascular events (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.77–0.81, per 1.0 mmol/L reduction).
ctt-collaborators.implications: These individual-participant meta-analysis results support that lowering LDL cholesterol with statin therapy reduces major vascular events per 1.0 mmol/L reduction (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.77–0.81) and that similar proportional reductions are seen even in lower baseline-risk groups (eg, RR 0.62 [99% CI 0.47–0.81] for <5% 5-year risk). The document also reports no evidence of increased cancer incidence (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.96–1.04) or cancer mortality (RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.93–1.06) per 1.0 mmol/L reduction, but it does not provide trial-level estimates for individual statin regimens beyond these pooled rate ratios and stated absolute reductions.

engage-af-timi-48.bottom_line: During the treatment period, stroke or systemic embolic event occurred at 1.18% per year with high-dose edoxaban vs 1.50% per year with warfarin (hazard ratio vs. warfarin, 0.79; 97.5% confidence interval [CI], 0.63 to 0.99).
engage-af-timi-48.implications: In this trial, during the treatment period, high-dose edoxaban had a lower annualized rate of stroke or systemic embolic event than warfarin (1.18% vs 1.50% per year; hazard ratio, 0.79; 97.5% CI, 0.63 to 0.99), while low-dose edoxaban had a similar rate to warfarin (1.61% vs 1.50% per year; hazard ratio, 1.07; 97.5% CI, 0.87 to 1.31). Both edoxaban regimens had lower annualized major bleeding than warfarin (2.75% and 1.61% vs 3.43% per year). These numbers support conclusions about comparative efficacy and bleeding rates as defined and adjudicated in this study, and do not by themselves establish effects outside the study population or beyond the trial’s defined treatment/analysis periods.

dapt.bottom_line: In patients with drug-eluting stents, continued thienopyridine plus aspirin vs placebo plus aspirin from 12 to 30 months reduced stent thrombosis (hazard ratio, 0.29 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.48]).

The document also reports an elevated risk of stent thrombosis and myocardial infarction during the 3 months after thienopyridine discontinuation in both groups, and does not establish effects for other stent types or non-thienopyridine P2Y12 inhibitors.

topcat.bottom_line: In TOPCAT, spironolactone vs placebo did not significantly reduce the primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 1.04).

improve-it.bottom_line: In IMPROVE-IT, simvastatin–ezetimibe vs simvastatin monotherapy reduced the primary composite end point (hazard ratio, 0.936; 95% confidence interval, 0.89 to 0.99).
improve-it.implications: These data support that, in patients after acute coronary syndrome, adding ezetimibe to simvastatin (vs simvastatin alone) was associated with a lower 7-year Kaplan–Meier rate of the primary composite end point (32.7% vs 34.7%) with hazard ratio 0.936 (95% CI, 0.89 to 0.99). pegasus-timi-54.bottom_line: In patients with a myocardial infarction 1 to 3 years earlier, ticagrelor (90 mg or 60 mg twice daily) vs placebo reduced cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (hazard ratio 0.85 [95% CI, 0.75 to 0.96] for 90 mg; 0.84 [95% CI, 0.74 to 0.95] for 60 mg).
pegasus-timi-54.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, ticagrelor 90 mg or 60 mg twice daily (on background aspirin) lowered the 3-year Kaplan–Meier rate of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (7.85% and 7.77% vs 9.04%; hazard ratios 0.85 and 0.84 with 95% CIs excluding 1.0), while increasing TIMI major bleeding (2.60% and 2.30% vs 1.06%; hazard ratios 2.69 and 2.32). The reported rates of fatal bleeding or nonfatal intracranial hemorrhage were <1% over 3 years in all groups, and death from any cause did not differ significantly by dose vs placebo (1.00 [0.86–1.16] and 0.89 [0.76–1.04]).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with three parallel groups (ticagrelor 90 mg, ticagrelor 60 mg, placebo) and background aspirin.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned, in a double-blind 1:1:1 fashion, 21,162 patients who had had a myocardial infarction 1 to 3 years earlier to ticagrelor at a dose of 90 mg twice daily, ticagrelor at a dose of 60 mg twice daily, or placebo.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke; primary safety end point was TIMI major bleeding.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke. The primary safety end point was Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) major bleeding.

major_points.text: TIMI major bleeding was higher with ticagrelor vs placebo, while intracranial hemorrhage or fatal bleeding rates were reported as similar across groups in the abstract.
major_points.quote: Rates of TIMI major bleeding were higher with ticagrelor (2.60% with 90 mg and 2.30% with 60 mg) than with placebo (1.06%) (P<0.001 for each dose vs. placebo); the rates of intracranial hemorrhage or fatal bleeding in the three groups were 0.63%, 0.71%, and 0.60%, respectively.

major_points.text: Premature discontinuation of treatment occurred more often in ticagrelor groups than placebo over the duration of the trial.
major_points.quote: The proportions of patients in each group who discontinued treatment prematurely over the duration of the trial were 32.0% in the group that received 90 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, 28.7% in the group that received 60 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, and 21.4% in the placebo group

major_points.text: Dyspnea occurred more frequently with ticagrelor and more often led to study-drug discontinuation than placebo.

pioneer-af-pci.bottom_line: In PIONEER AF-PCI, clinically significant bleeding was lower with rivaroxaban-based regimens than with dose-adjusted vitamin K antagonist plus DAPT (group 1 vs. group 3 hazard ratio 0.59 [95% CI, 0.47 to 0.76]; group 2 vs. group 3 hazard ratio 0.63 [95% CI, 0.50 to 0.80]).
pioneer-af-pci.implications: These data support that, over 12 months, rivaroxaban-based strategies (group 1: 16.8%; group 2: 18.0%) were associated with lower clinically significant bleeding than vitamin K antagonist plus DAPT (26.7%), with hazard ratios 0.59 (95% CI, 0.47 to 0.76) and 0.63 (95% CI, 0.50 to 0.80). For major adverse cardiovascular events, observed rates were 6.5%, 5.6%, and 6.0% with hazard ratios 1.08 (95% CI, 0.69–1.68) and 0.93 (95% CI, 0.59–1.48), and the document states broad confidence intervals and lack of power, so firm conclusions regarding efficacy are not supported by these results.

re-dual-pci.bottom_line: In RE-DUAL PCI, dual therapy with dabigatran 110 mg plus a P2Y12 inhibitor resulted in a lower incidence of the primary end point than triple therapy with warfarin (hazard ratio, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.42 to 0.63).
re-dual-pci.implications: Based on the reported primary end-point rates and hazard ratio (15.4% vs 26.9%; hazard ratio, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.42 to 0.63), the results support that dabigatran 110-mg dual therapy was associated with lower major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than warfarin-based triple therapy in this trial; based on the composite efficacy end point (13.7% vs 13.4%; hazard ratio, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.84 to 1.29; P = 0.005 for noninferiority), the data support noninferiority for that composite when dual-therapy groups were combined, but do not establish superiority for efficacy.

afire.bottom_line: In AFIRE, rivaroxaban monotherapy was noninferior to rivaroxaban plus a single antiplatelet agent for the primary efficacy end point (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.95).
afire.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, rivaroxaban monotherapy achieved noninferior rates of the primary composite end point versus combination therapy (4.14% vs 5.75% per patient-year; hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.95) and had lower major bleeding rates (1.62% vs 2.76% per patient-year; hazard ratio, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.89). The document also notes early trial termination for higher all-cause death in the combination-therapy group and that early termination may overestimate efficacy data, so the magnitude of benefit should be interpreted with that caveat.

augustus.bottom_line: In patients with atrial fibrillation and a recent acute coronary syndrome or PCI treated with a P2Y12 inhibitor, apixaban resulted in less major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than a vitamin K antagonist (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.58 to 0.81).
augustus.implications: These data support the conclusion that, over 6 months in this trial population, apixaban (vs vitamin K antagonist) reduced ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (10.5% vs. 14.7%; hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.81) and reduced death or hospitalization (23.5% vs. 27.4%; hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.93), while death or ischemic event was not significantly different (hazard ratio, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.75–1.16). Aspirin (vs placebo) increased bleeding (16.1% vs. 9.0%; hazard ratio, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.59 to 2.24) and did not significantly change death or hospitalization (hazard ratio, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.96 to 1.21). The document notes the trial was not designed to detect small differences in less common individual ischemic outcomes.

dapa-hf.bottom_line: In DAPA-HF, dapagliflozin vs placebo reduced the primary composite of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.85).
dapa-hf.implications: These data show that, over a median of 18.2 months, dapagliflozin compared with placebo was associated with a lower incidence of the primary composite outcome (16.3% vs. 21.2%; hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.85; P<0.001) and lower all-cause mortality (11.6% vs. 13.9%; hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.97), while selected adverse events of interest such as volume depletion (7.5% vs. 6.8%) and renal adverse events (6.5% vs. 7.2%) were reported at similar frequencies; the trial also reports results were similar in patients with and without diabetes.

east-afnet-4.bottom_line: Early rhythm control vs usual care reduced the first primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.79; 96% confidence interval, 0.66 to 0.94).
east-afnet-4.implications: In patients with early atrial fibrillation and cardiovascular conditions, the strategy of early rhythm control was associated with fewer first-primary-outcome events than usual care (3.9 vs 5.0 per 100 person-years; hazard ratio, 0.79; 96% confidence interval, 0.66 to 0.94). The mean number of nights spent in the hospital did not differ significantly between groups (5.8±21.9 vs 5.1±15.5 days per year; P = 0.23). The primary composite safety outcome occurred in similar proportions (16.6% vs 16.0), while serious adverse events of special interest related to rhythm-control therapy were more frequent with early rhythm control (4.9% vs 1.4%).

advor.bottom_line: Acetazolamide (500 mg once daily) added to intravenous loop diuretics increased successful decongestion within 3 days versus placebo (risk ratio, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.17 to 1.82).
advor.implications: In this trial of 519 randomized patients with acute decompensated heart failure and clinical volume overload, adding acetazolamide to standardized intravenous loop diuretics increased the incidence of successful decongestion within 3 days (42.2% vs. 30.5%; risk ratio, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.17 to 1.82). The trial does not show a difference in the 3-month composite of death from any cause or rehospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.48), and reported prespecified safety events during the treatment phase were similar between groups (e.g., hypokalemia 5.5% vs 3.9%; hypotension 6.6% vs 3.5%).

major_points.text: Multicenter, parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in acute decompensated heart failure with volume overload.
major_points.quote: In this multicenter, parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, we assigned patients with acute decompensated heart failure, clinical signs of volume overload

deliver.bottom_line: In patients with heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of more than 40%, dapagliflozin vs placebo reduced the primary composite of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.92).
deliver.implications: These results support that dapagliflozin, compared with placebo, lowered the risk of the composite of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.92) in this trial population. The cardiovascular-death component alone was not shown to be reduced with statistical certainty (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.05). Serious adverse events were reported at similar proportions in the two groups (43.5% vs 45.5%).

dapa-mi.bottom_line: In patients with acute MI without prior diabetes or chronic heart failure, dapagliflozin vs placebo improved the primary hierarchical composite outcome (win ratio, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.20 to 1.50).

empact-mi.bottom_line: Empagliflozin 10 mg daily versus placebo after acute myocardial infarction did not significantly lower the risk of first hospitalization for heart failure or death from any cause (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.06).
empact-mi.implications: The reported hazard ratio for the primary composite outcome (0.90; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.06; P = 0.21) does not support a statistically significant reduction in first hospitalization for heart failure or death from any cause with empagliflozin versus placebo in this trial, while the reported component outcome shows fewer first hospitalizations for heart failure with empagliflozin (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.60 to 0.98) and similar all-cause death (hazard ratio, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.19).

digit-hf.bottom_line: In patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction, digitoxin vs placebo reduced the primary composite of death from any cause or first hospital admission for worsening heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98).
digit-hf.implications: These data support that, in the modified intention-to-treat population, digitoxin was associated with a lower hazard of the composite endpoint of death from any cause or first hospital admission for worsening heart failure than placebo (hazard ratio 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98; P=0.03). The confidence interval for death from any cause includes 1.0 (hazard ratio, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.69 to 1.07), so the document does not establish superiority for all-cause mortality alone; it reports noninferiority (threshold 1.303; P<0.001). Serious adverse events occurred in 4.7% with digitoxin vs 2.8% with placebo.

decision.bottom_line: In DECISION, low-dose digoxin versus placebo did not significantly reduce the primary composite of total worsening heart failure events and cardiovascular death (rate ratio 0.81; 95% CI 0.61–1.07, P = 0.133).
decision.implications: With 238 versus 291 primary-outcome events (rate ratio 0.81; 95% CI 0.61–1.07; P = 0.133), this trial does not support a statistically significant reduction in the composite endpoint with low-dose digoxin versus placebo over the reported follow-up. The confidence interval includes no effect and a potential reduction. Safety signals reported as serious adverse events were similar overall (19.9 vs 18.3 events per 100 patient-years; rate ratio 1.09; 95% CI 0.86–1.37).
